Subject: Access logs: export formats, retention, and deletion process

Hi Kimberly,

We have a renewal audit coming up and the security team has a couple of specific asks around access/audit logs:

- What retention windows do you support for access logs (hosted + enterprise + private)?
- Can we get a full export of our tenant's access logs (all API calls + admin actions) in a single deliverable? Preferred formats are JSONL or Parquet.
- During legal hold, what is your process to preserve vs. delete records? How do you prove deletion after the hold is lifted?
- What is the expected SLA for scheduled exports (hours/days) and do you provide checksums or manifests?

Can you point me to a runbook/detail we can include in the audit package?

Thanks,

Hi Angela — thanks for the clear list. High level answers below; I attached our export playbook (v1.2) and a sample schema. Marissa and Jonas are copied for technical confirmation and SLA estimates.

Quick summary:
- Retention: Hosted default 90 days; enterprise plan configurable up to 540 days (13 months) depending on commitment; private deployments are customer-controlled.
- Export formats: JSONL (preferred), CSV, and Parquet supported for bulk extracts. We deliver compressed archives (gz or zip).
- Legal hold: we snapshot tenant data to a preservation bucket (immutable snapshot) and tag it with a hold ID; deletion is blocked until hold release. After release and deletion, we provide a signed deletion manifest (SHA256 checksums, timestamps).
- SLA: Standard scheduled exports: 48–72 hours; urgent export (approved escalation): 4–12 hours depending on size.

Next steps: can we schedule a short call to confirm export scope (time range, object types) and whether you need on-prem handoff or secure SFTP delivery?

Attachments: export_playbook_v1.2.pdf, access_log_schema.csv

Regards,

Kim/Jonas/Rishi — answers below, based on current platform behaviour and enterprise playbook. Happy to turn this into a one-page FAQ for the audit.

1) Size estimate: typical event ~1.2KB compressed (JSONL gz). For your example (500k/month): ~600MB/month compressed, ~7.2GB/year compressed. Parquet tends to be smaller for repeated schema fields (~40-60% size reduction) but depends on cardinality.

2) Runbook (summary):
- Initiate export ticket (Ops) with tenant ID and time range.
- Quiesce routing for 30–60 mins if export window requires consistent snapshot.
- Create immutable snapshot in region (snapshot ID + hold ID if legal hold).
- Stream events to export worker -> write JSONL + manifest (SHA256 per file) -> compress -> upload to delivery target.
- Post-delivery: if legal hold active, retention flag set; otherwise schedule deletion job.
- Deletion step: run erase job that removes tenant records from active shards, mark manifest deleted, and produce a signed deletion manifest (timestamp + signer: Trust Ops lead).

Signatures/manifests: we provide a signed PDF manifest (HSM-backed signature) with file list, checksums, and job run metadata.

3) Schema & PII: Default export redacts browser-level cookies and ephemeral session tokens. Fields that are always present in JSONL: timestamp, request_id, principal_id, action, resource, region, source_ip (anonymized if requested), user_agent (optional). Parquet export will flatten arrays and may drop raw headers unless requested. We can do custom redaction per contract.

4) EU deliveries: we encrypt at rest with customer-managed keys (CKMS) for enterprise EU tenants. For cross-border egress, we require a Data Transfer Addendum signed by security + legal; standard encryption over SFTP/HTTPS is applied.

Estimated SLA: 48 hours for standard exports under 5GB; 72 hours for 5–50GB; >50GB escalate to 72–120 hours and require logistics planning.

I'll draft a one-page audit FAQ and include the runbook steps and sample manifest.

Marissa
Engineering Manager, Ops | Redwood Inference

Adding a couple of operational clarifications for Finvero:

- If we perform a legal-hold snapshot for EU tenants, snapshots remain in-region and are written to an immutable bucket for the duration of the hold. Exports for legal discovery are run from that snapshot to avoid cross-border reads.
- Deletion proof: we keep a deletion audit that includes job id, worker nodes involved, shard list, and tombstone markers. The signed deletion manifest links to that internal audit id (we can include that id in the PDF manifest).
- Scheduling: best practice is to schedule exports during a low-traffic window; we recommend a 2-hour maintenance window to avoid partial KV cache inconsistencies.

I can commit Ops time for a one-hour prep call and a 2-hour export window if Finvero confirms time slots — that should cover both snapshot and delivery.

-Jonas

Hi Angela — following up with the consolidated answers and next steps. Please see the attached playbook and sample export. Key points for your audit pack:

- Retention: Hosted default 90 days, enterprise configurable up to 540 days; private deployments are controlled by customer.
- Formats: JSONL (event-per-line) is the default; Parquet available for columnar efficiency. We provide compressed archives + manifest (SHA256) and an HSM-backed signed PDF manifest on completion.
- Legal hold: we snapshot and set a hold ID; deletion is blocked until release. After release we run the erase job and provide a signed deletion manifest linking to internal audit IDs.
- SLA & scheduling: Standard deliveries: 48–72 hours for <50GB. Ops can support a 2-hour export window (recommended).

Next steps: 1) Can you confirm the time range and preferred delivery method (SFTP + AES-256, AWS S3 presigned link, or direct in-region transfer)? 2) Do you need a custom redaction policy? 3) If you want an expedited export, please mark as urgent and provide PO/authorization so we loop Legal.
